Afro-Caribbean or African Caribbean people are Caribbean people who trace their full or partial ancestry to Sub-Saharan Africa . The majority of the modern Afro-Caribbean people descend from the West and Central Africans taken as slaves to the colonial Caribbean via the trans-Atlantic slave trade between the 15th and 19th centuries to work primarily on various sugar plantations and in domestic households. Other names for the ethnic group include Black Caribbean , Afro- or Black West Indian , or Afro- or Black Antillean . The term West Indian Creole has also been used to refer to Afro-Caribbean people, [ 30 ] as well as other ethnic and racial groups in the region, [ 31 ] [ 32 ] [ 33 ] though there remains debate about its use to refer to Afro-Caribbean people specifically. [ 34 ] [ 35 ] The term Afro-Caribbean was not coined by Caribbean people themselves but was first used by European Americans in the late 1960s. [ 36 ]
